attacker_pocs.name: bytes-hint-and-payload-overflow
attacker_pocs.why: A normal scanline EXR whose bytes attribute has both a type hint and a payload (written by OutputFile, read by MultiPartInputFile). extract_attr_bytes allocates the payload only, then sequential_read copies value_size bytes, which still includes the hint, so memcpy writes past the heap buffer.

role_a_rationale: Zero-length bytes values no longer call memcpy with a NULL source: BytesAttribute skips the copy when size is 0 (constructor, copy, copyValueFrom, readValueFrom), and the core reader skips the hint and payload reads when those lengths are 0 and rejects a hint longer than the value. That stops the null-pointer memcpy when MultiPartInputFile builds a BytesAttribute from an empty payload. The payload read still passes value_size (bytes after the length word, including the hint that was already consumed) instead of bytes_length, so a valid attribute that has both a hint and a payload overflows the payload allocation. Empty payload, hint-only, and data-only attributes still round-trip.
